$schema_note: task-079. The friendly ("hero-side"/retinue) build-variety layer: chassis x weapon-archetype x projectile x modification x ability x origin-world, combinatorially producing hundreds of unit builds from a handful of axis tables — the generalization of docs/data/unit-types.json's two hand-written types (spearmen, archers) into a data-driven space. Decisions + rationale, the constraint reasoning, the worked examples and the open questions all live in docs/design/hero-build-variety.md — this file is the raw axis/constraint/rule data only. Columns/units/ranges: hero-builds.schema.md. Simulation-space only (owner, 2026-07-29): nothing here is UE-DataTable-imported or runtime-read yet. All values are PROTOTYPE DIALS (first pass, unmeasured) except where a field's note says CITED and names the source — same status as docs/data/unit-types.json and docs/data/economy.json.

reachable_build_count.raw_product_formula: chassis(8) x weapon_archetypes(10) x projectiles(10) x (modifications(6)+none) x (abilities(6)+none) x origin_worlds(6) = 8x10x10x7x7x6
reachable_build_count.raw_product_note: The full combinatorial space with NO chassis coherence constraint applied — every chassis could roll every weapon/projectile/mod/ability/origin. This is the number that would let an archer chassis legally roll a shield-wall ability, which the owner explicitly ruled out ('somewhat themed consistently to their character view').
reachable_build_count.legal_count_note: task-090 correction: 999 (the old value) multiplied each chassis's legal_weapons x legal_projectiles as if every legal weapon could fire every one of that chassis's legal projectiles — it counted incoherent builds (a Cleave Melee Sweep firing a Shrapnel Spread, a Continuous Beam firing a Fletched Arrow) that Scripts/sim/variety.py now refuses to roll (see weapon_projectile_coupling_note below). Corrected formula: sum over chassis of [ sum over that chassis's legal_weapons of |chassis.legal_projectiles ∩ {p : projectiles[p].travel_type in weapon.legal_travel_types}| ] x (legal_modifications+1 for 'none') x (legal_abilities+1 for 'none') x legal_origin_worlds. Verified by the same committed-nowhere scratch-script method as before (docs/design/hero-build-variety.md 'Simulation notes'), not hand-arithmetic. task-098 raised this from 729 to 774: archer's legal_modifications gained piercing_rounds (135 -> 180 per_chassis, the only chassis touched — see docs/sim/DIFFERENTIATION.md's task-098 section for why), everything else unchanged. 774 is 3.29% of the raw product — still solidly 'hundreds'. Both calibration_builds and both worked_example_builds remain exactly legal under the new constraint (checked by hand, see docs/design/hero-build-variety.md); neither uses a modification, so archer's new 3rd legal_modification doesn't touch them.
reachable_build_count.per_chassis_note: task-090: no longer a uniform legal_weapons x legal_projectiles product per chassis — each legal weapon now contributes only the count of that chassis's legal_projectiles whose travel_type is in the weapon's own legal_travel_types (weapon_projectile_coupling_note). Archer's weapon-projectile pairs are still 5 (precision_longbow: 2 arc-compatible + arcing_aoe_lobber: 2 arc-compatible + beam_continuous: 1 hitscan-compatible), but task-098 added piercing_rounds as archer's 3rd legal_modification, so the '(legal_modifications+1)' term rose from 3 to 4: 5 x 4 x 3 abilities(+none) x 3 origins = 180 (was 135 pre-task-098). Line Breaker and Beastcaller are 54 because each of their two legal weapons resolves to exactly 1 compatible projectile (2 pairs, not 4). Gunner, Arcane Caster, Combat Engineer and Siege Artillerist are 108 — in each of those four chassis, both legal weapons happen to already be travel-type-compatible with both of the chassis's legal projectiles (4 pairs), so the coupling constraint removed nothing there. Archer is still the widest chassis by design (see original 'RPG archer'/'laser cannon' rationale below), now wider still after task-098's armor-gate fix (docs/design/hero-build-variety.md sec 2b).

weapon_projectile_coupling_note: task-090. A build's legal projectile set = chassis.legal_projectiles ∩ {p : projectiles[p].travel_type in weapon_archetypes[weapon].legal_travel_types} — reuses `projectiles.<id>.travel_type`'s own enum (hitscan/ballistic_arc/physical_straight/melee_instant/homing) directly, no second taxonomy. Chosen shape: a `legal_travel_types` array added to EACH `weapon_archetypes.<id>` row (not a standalone top-level weapon_projectile_legality map), because it reads next to the weapon field it constrains — the same place every other weapon-specific fact already lives — and because chain_bounce_shot genuinely needs TWO travel types (hitscan for chain_bolt/slug_round/energy_beam AND physical_straight for shrapnel_spread — its own note already says 'ricochet slug'/'barbed boomerang', i.e. a bounced physical shot as much as a chained energy one), so a single travel-type-per-weapon scalar wouldn't fit every row; an array does. Scripts/sim/variety.py picks the weapon first, then rng.choice()s from this intersection, and RAISES if the intersection is empty for a rolled chassis/weapon pair rather than silently falling back to the chassis's full legal_projectiles list — an empty intersection means the data is wrong, not that the roll should quietly degrade. Every existing chassis/weapon pair was checked by hand before this shipped and has a non-empty intersection (docs/design/hero-build-variety.md 'Simulation notes' has the full per-chassis arithmetic); no chassis.legal_projectiles list needed to change to make that true.

archer.note: CALIBRATION CHASSIS — base stats are an exact carry-over of unit-types.json's Archers row (hp/armor/move_speed_scale), so the existing type stays reachable as a point in this space (see calibration_builds.archers). task-098: gained piercing_rounds as a legal_modification (see docs/design/hero-build-variety.md sec 2b) — calibration_builds.archers itself keeps modification:null and is untouched.

gunner.note: New chassis. High rate-of-fire, low per-shot damage skirmisher — the sustained-pressure counterpart to Archer's precision shot.

line_breaker.note: CALIBRATION CHASSIS — base stats are an exact carry-over of unit-types.json's Spearmen row, so the existing type stays reachable as a point in this space (see calibration_builds.spearmen). Generalizes 'the melee wall' role Spearmen already occupy.

skirmisher.note: New chassis. Fast, low-HP dual-wielder (blades or sidearms) — the mobility/flanking counterpart to Line Breaker's wall.

arcane_caster.note: New chassis. Sustained-beam / chain-effect caster — fragile, high-uptime damage rather than burst.

combat_engineer.note: New chassis. Sturdier, moderate-armor sustained-fire support line — the 'holds a position and keeps shooting' role.

beastcaller.note: New chassis. Organic/summon-flavored melee-leaning hybrid, moderate HP and light armor.

siege_artillerist.note: New chassis. Slow, huge-hit, huge-min-range backline — cannot function at short range at all, the deliberate opposite of Line Breaker.

precision_longbow.note: CALIBRATION ROW — CITED. rate_of_fire/damage_per_shot chosen so dps and swing_interval exactly reproduce unit-types.json's Archers (dps 18, swing_interval 0.9) and entity-tiers.md §2.2's own stated Archer blow value (16.2 = 16.2 damage_per_shot x 1/0.9 rate_of_fire).

cleave_melee_sweep.note: CALIBRATION ROW — CITED. rate_of_fire/damage_per_shot chosen so dps and swing_interval exactly reproduce unit-types.json's Spearmen (dps 30, swing_interval 0.9) and entity-tiers.json design_constants.reference_blow_value (27.0 = Militia's blow, the system's own stated balance anchor).

arcing_aoe_lobber.note: PROTOTYPE DIAL. The owner's own named example ('RPG archer... shooting explosives that do damage in an area'). Slow, single heavy hit plus splash radius, deliberately un-usable at point-blank (min_range 120) — a lobbed weapon can't hit what's standing on it.

beam_continuous.note: PROTOTYPE DIAL. The owner's other named example ('the next a laser cannon'). Modeled as a very fast tick rate approximating a sustained channel — same steady-state dps class as Precision Longbow, but the opposite cadence shape (many small hits vs. one big one), so it reads as a genuinely different weapon, not a reskinned longbow.

rapid_skirmish_blaster.note: PROTOTYPE DIAL. Highest rate_of_fire in the roster, lowest damage_per_shot, short range — a close-pressure suppression weapon, not a sniping tool.

chain_bounce_shot.note: PROTOTYPE DIAL. Hits a primary target and chains to 2 more (targets_per_shot 3) without any aoe_radius — a genuinely different multi-target shape from an AoE weapon (discrete chain vs. area), meant to be paired with the 'pierce' projectile resolve_type. task-098: damage_per_shot raised 14.0->19.0, see docs/design/hero-build-variety.md sec 2b (armor-gate rationale) — already legal on beastcaller alongside piercing_rounds, so this was the cheaper lever than opening a new chassis.

dual_strike_melee.note: PROTOTYPE DIAL. Fast dual-hit melee, no cleave beyond its own two strikes (targets_per_shot 2) — the mobility-focused counterpart to Cleave Melee Sweep's wide, slower cleave.

shotgun_spread.note: PROTOTYPE DIAL. Short range, wide instantaneous cone (targets_per_shot 4, no aoe_radius — the cone is resolved as discrete simultaneous targets, not a lingering area) — a burst-alpha weapon for a unit that gets in close and unloads.

siege_artillery.note: PROTOTYPE DIAL. The largest single hit and largest aoe_radius in the roster, the slowest rate_of_fire (a shot every ~6.7s), and the only min_range that excludes most of the map's mid-range band (300uu) — cannot function as anything but a fixed backline piece.

turret_autocannon.note: PROTOTYPE DIAL. Sustained mid-rate fire hitting 2 targets_per_shot with no aoe_radius (small discrete cleave, not splash) — the 'holds a line and keeps two targets suppressed' support gun.

focus_optic.note: Trades rate of fire for range — the 'scope' archetype.

overcharge_core.note: Trades rate of fire for damage per shot — bigger, slower hits.

piercing_rounds.note: Reduces the VICTIM's Armor (entity-tiers.md §2.2's EffectiveBlow formula) by a flat 4 before the ArmorChipFloor clamp is applied. NOT consumable by Scripts/sim/combat_model.py today — needs a one-line extension (EffectiveBlow = max(AttackerBlow - max(Victim.Armor - ArmorPenetrationFlat, 0), ArmorChipFloor)), see hero-build-variety.md's sim-consumability section.

wide_choke.note: Trades range for one more simultaneous target.

rally_cry.representable_note: Periodic aura, +12% dps to allies within 300uu for 4s every 12s (33% uptime). Approximable in the point-target model ONLY as a flat expected-value multiplier (1 + 0.12 x 4/12 = 1.04x) applied to nearby allies — not a per-tick positional effect, and not usable at all in the pooled wave-attrition model, which has no per-unit position.

camouflage_strike.representable_note: First shot from stealth deals +200% damage, then the bonus is gone for the rest of the fight. A one-shot burst event has no representation in a steady-state DPS number — encoding it as a number the sim would silently misuse (e.g. folding it into average dps) is exactly what the brief asked NOT to do.

shield_regen.representable_note: Regenerates 4% max_hp/sec after 3s out of combat. Neither combat model tracks in/out-of-combat state or time-varying HP outside the attrition tick itself — no field to attach this to without adding a new primitive.

last_stand.representable_note: +50% dps while below 25% HP. State-dependent on an individual soldier's remaining HP; the point-target model tracks only the TARGET's HP, and the wave-attrition model tracks pooled HP per subgroup, not per-soldier — there is no per-soldier HP state to threshold against.

chain_reactor.representable_note: On kill, next attack's swing_interval is halved. Representable ONLY in the point-target model, where one attacker's kill rate against the target is a computable quantity (task-080 would derive it, not this file) — NOT representable in the wave-attrition model, where kills aren't attributed to individual attackers.

guardian_angel.representable_note: Once per fight, prevents one squadmate's death within 400uu. Not a stat-block field at all — representable ONLY as a flat +1 adjustment to the wave-attrition model's final survivor count per instance present in the roster, a post-hoc headcount correction, not a DPS/HP number.

iron_reach.flavor_note: Medieval-martial — steel, siege engines, banners. The default/legacy world; Spearmen and Archers' native origin (calibration_builds both use this).

glass_tide.flavor_note: Crystal/psionic — refracted light weapons, mind-bent constructs.

origin_worlds_note: WorkingNameOnly, same convention entity-tiers.json already uses for its brood_* rows — docs/narrative/FLAME-FOUNDATION.md names no worlds yet (WORLD.md is SUPERSEDED, not cited). These six exist so the origin-world axis and its synergy rules are checkable now; naming/fiction is a Narrative request (hero-build-variety.md).

synergy_rules.note: Machine-checkable roster-level rules. Each condition is evaluated against a ROLLED ROSTER (a list of resolved builds, each carrying its axis picks + its build_stat_block, see hero-builds.schema.md). `scope` says which units in the roster the effect applies to. Rule 4 is the required anti-synergy/cost — it directly opposes rule 1 (Kindred Ranks) so 'roll one of every world' is not simply strictly better than 'commit to a few worlds'.

rules.description: A roster whose single most-common origin_world makes up at least half the roster reads as a disciplined, drilled-together force.
Ashworks gunsmiths and Deep Static coil-engineers cross-pollinate: forges learn to etch circuitry, coil-labs learn to cast barrels.
Two or more Rally Cry banners compound across the whole line, not just their own local radius.

ANTI-SYNERGY / COST. Five or more of the six origin-worlds present in one roster means too many mutually unfamiliar drill traditions standing shoulder to shoulder — coordination friction, not strength. Directly opposes kindred_ranks: maximizing world diversity is not simply better than committing to a concentrated or paired roster.

calibration_builds.note: Verifies the current two shipped types (docs/data/unit-types.json) remain reachable, exactly, as points in this space (see hero-build-variety.md 'Simulation notes' for the script that checked this).

worked_example_builds.note: Same chassis (Archer), same base HP/Armor/move, radically different fight shape — the owner's own paired example. See hero-build-variety.md for the side-by-side stat block table and read.
